rows.label: Concept
rows.text: **Collinear** vectors share a line: b = λa, tested by **a × b = 0** (sin θ = 0) or equal component ratios. **Coplanar** vectors share a plane: tested by **[a b c] = a·(b × c) = 0** (zero volume) or the combination form c = λa + μb. The two conditions are dependence in geometric dress — two-vector dependence is parallelism, three-vector dependence is coplanarity — and two vectors are *always* coplanar, which is why…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - Collinear: b = λa ⟺ a × b = 0 ⟺ a₁/b₁ = a₂/b₂ = a₃/b₃ - Coplanar: [a b c] = a·(b × c) = 0 ⟺ c = λa + μb - Points collinear: (b − a) × (c − a) = 0; four points coplanar: [AB AC AD] = 0

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "a, b, c are coplanar iff a.(b x c) = 0; a, b are collinear iff a x b = 0."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The connecting-vector rule*** — for points, subtract first: AB = b - a and AC = c - a; only their parallelism says the points share a line.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Covers only: collinear, non-collinear vectors, coplanar, non-coplanar vectors (within Vectors).  ·  Out of scope here: topics of neighbouring units in Mathematics — don't mix them.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Sharing a Line or a Plane **Collinear** vectors lie along one line; **coplanar** vectors lie in one plane. The theorems give algebraic tests: a cross-product zero test for collinearity, a scalar-triple-product zero test for coplanarity, and the linear-combination characterisations that tie this topic to dependence.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Collinear vectors - **Definition:** vectors a, b are collinear if they are parallel to the same line — equivalently **b = λa** for some scalar λ (non-zero vectors). - **Theorem (cross test):** a, b are collinear ⟺ **a × b = 0** (since |a × b| = |a||b|sin θ and sin θ = 0 exactly when parallel).…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Two vectors: equal component ratios (watch zeros). Three vectors: 3x3 determinant = 0. Points: form AB, AC first, then test.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB-style (2m): Show that a = î + ĵ + k̂ and b = 2î + 2ĵ + 2k̂ are collinear.** — **Ratio test:** a₁/b₁ = 1/2, a₂/b₂ = 1/2, a₃/b₃ = 1/2 — all three ratios are equal, so **b = 2a**: one vector is a scalar multiple of the other, which is exactly collinearity.…  ·  **NEB-style (3m): Show that the vectors a = î − ĵ + k̂, b = 2î + ĵ − k̂, c = î − 3ĵ + 3k̂ are coplanar.** — **Triple product test:** three vectors are coplanar iff [a b c] = a·(b × c) = 0, computed as the determinant of components: det |1 −1 1; 2 1 −1; 1 −3 3| = 1[(1)(3) − (−1)(−3)] − (−1)[(2)(3) − (−1)(1)] + 1[(2)(−3) − (1)(1)] = 1(3 −…

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: The tests are geometry in algebra: cross product zero kills sin th (line sharing), triple product zero kills volume (plane sharing).

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Collinear vectors: parallel to one line; b = la for scalar l; test a x b = 0; component ratios a1/b1 = a2/b2 = a3/b3 (non-zero components). Coplanar vectors: parallel to one plane; test [a b c] = a.(b x c) = 0; equivalently c = la + mb. Points A, B, C collinear iff AB || AC i.e. (b-a) x (c-a) = 0.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Collinearity and coplanarity are dependence wearing geometry: b = la is two-vector dependence, c = la + mb is three-vector dependence.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **NEB-style (2m): State and prove the condition for three points A, B, C to be collinear.** — **Condition:** A, B, C are collinear ⟺ **AB × AC = 0**, i.e. (b − a) × (c − a) = 0 in position vectors.…

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 3. Scientific Definitions | Term | Scientific meaning | Example | |---|---|---| | **Collinear vectors** | Parallel to one common line | a and 3a | | **Coplanar vectors** | Parallel to one common plane | î, ĵ, î + 2ĵ | | **Cross test** | a × b = 0 detects collinearity | sin θ = 0 | | **Triple product test** | [a b c] = 0 detects coplanarity | flattened parallelepiped |  ·  ## 4. Detailed Explanation ### 4.1 Why the tests work - Collinearity kills sin θ (cross product magnitude); coplanarity kills the volume (scalar triple product). Both tests are geometric facts wearing algebra. ### 4.2 Free vectors vs points - Vectors are free (translatable); points are not.…  ·  ## 5. Comparison Tables **Collinearity vs coplanarity** | Basis | Collinear | Coplanar | |---|---|---| | applies to | two vectors (line) | three vectors (plane) | | algebraic test | a × b = 0 | [a b c] = 0 | | combination form | b = λa | c = λa + μb | | geometric image | flattened to a line | flattened to a plane |

Common Confusions **Two vectors are always coplanar:** any two directions define a plane — coplanarity is a *three-vector* condition.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **a × b = 0 also when a or b is 0:** the zero vector is trivially collinear with everything; the test still holds.  ·  **Point collinearity needs connecting vectors:** check AB ∥ AC, not the position vectors a, b, c themselves.  ·  ## 7. Exam Application **NEB-style (3m): Show that the points with position vectors a = 2î − ĵ + k̂, b = 3î − 2ĵ + 2k̂, c = î − ĵ... are collinear (template).** — Form **AB = b − a** and **AC = c − a**; check whether AB = λAC by comparing components (or verify AB × AC = 0).…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **NEB-style (2m): Prove that î − ĵ + k̂, 2î + ĵ and −î + 3ĵ − k̂... coplanarity via triple product.** — Compute **[a b c]** as the 3×3 determinant of components; expansion gives a number. Zero ⟹ coplanar (one vector is a combination of the other two); non-zero ⟹ they span space.  ·  **NEB-style (2m): Show that a = î + ĵ + k̂, b = 2î + 2ĵ + 2k̂ are collinear.** — Component ratios: 1/2 = 1/2 = 1/2 ✓ — equal ratios, so **b = 2a** and the vectors are collinear. Equivalently a × b = 0: every component of the cross product vanishes because each pair of components is proportional.
